title: How to Enjoy Vietnamese Tea
intro: Ở một quán trà, Linh vừa pha vừa giải thích cho hai du khách: tráng ấm chén, dùng nước bao nhiêu độ, rót thế nào và mời trà sao cho lịch sự.

vocab.ex: She poured tea into four small cups.
Rinse the cups with hot water first.
These tea leaves come from the north.
Don't use boiling water for green tea.
The host made tea for everyone.
It's polite to say thank you.

transcript.t: Before we drink, I pour hot water over the teapot and the cups to warm them.
Warm cups keep the tea hot, and the smell of the tea comes out better.
And now you're adding the leaves?
Yes. Then I pour a little water and throw the first pour away. It rinses the leaves.
I see. How hot should the water be?
For this green tea, I use water at about eighty-five degrees, not boiling. Boiling water makes it bitter.
Not long, about thirty seconds. Then I fill every cup a little at a time, so each one has the same taste.
That's clever. Is there a polite way to drink it?
Give the first cups to the oldest people at the table, and use both hands when you offer a cup.
Then we sip slowly and say thank you!
Exactly. And you can say the tea is good. It makes the host happy.

listening.q: Why does Linh pour hot water over the cups first?
What happens to the first pour?
listening.why: ...throw the first pour away. It rinses the leaves.

listening.q: How hot is the water for this green tea?

a: The oldest people at the table
listening.why: Give the first cups to the oldest people at the table.

reading.q: According to Linh, why not use boiling water?
Why does Linh fill every cup a little at a time?
a: So each cup has the same taste
reading.why: ...so each one has the same taste.
you can say the tea is good. It makes the host happy.

write.prompt: Explain to a foreign friend, in 3 sentences, how to make or drink tea politely in Vietnam.
write.model: First, warm the teapot and the cups with hot water. Give the first cups to the oldest people and offer each cup with both hands. Then sip slowly and tell the host the tea is good.
